chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most hateful of people to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a man who bares the back of a Muslim without a right (to do so).'

key_terms.جَرَّدَ ظَهْرَ: Bared the back of (exposed to beating/humiliation)

ai.seo_question: Who is considered the most hated person to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith emphasizes the gravity of 'tajrid al-zahr' (stripping the back), a term historically referring to public flogging or humiliation, identifying the perpetrator as the most hated by Allah. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the dignity (karamah) of the individual Muslim, where unjust exposure to shame is considered a major sin akin to shedding blood.
